summary: A severance paper cannot take away unemployment, wage or vested retirement benefits.
realLife: The EEOC says to check that the agreement does not waive the right to file a charge, rights arising after signing, or release unemployment, workers' compensation, wage, COBRA or vested retirement benefits.
sources: U.S. EEOC, Q&A on waivers of discrimination claims in severance agreements: https://www.eeoc.gov/laws/guidance/qa-understanding-waivers-discrimination-claims-employee-severance-agreements
inGame: needs: severance agreements; unemployment pay can ride on the job-ended event. Scene: needs a producer for layoff-terms.

turns.summary: The paper hints that signing gives up unemployment pay, and the person is unsure.
pulledBy: a person who is worried or unsure
turns.writesBack: The person may delay signing, and a note says the terms were questioned.

turns.summary: The person asks a helper or friend what the paper can and cannot take away before signing.
pulledBy: a friend or relative who knows the rules
turns.writesBack: The tie to the helper gets closer, and the person signs with the benefits intact.

turns.summary: The person signs, then claims unemployment pay without trouble.
pulledBy: a person who knows the rules
turns.writesBack: Unemployment pay starts and the mood eases.
